title: Exhaustiveness of Threshold Scenarios for Colored Gaussian Graphical Models
statement: Let $G$ be a colored Gaussian graphical model with $I(G,n+1)=0$ and nonzero rank-$n$ elimination ideal $I(G,n)$. Must exactly one of the following mechanisms determine its thresholds: a nonvanishing signed sum of squares in $I(G,n)$, forcing $\operatorname{WMLT}(G)=\operatorname{MLT}(G)=n+1$; or a positive-definite covariance matrix whose sufficient statistics lie in $V(I(G,n))$, forcing $\operatorname{WMLT}(G)=n<\operatorname{MLT}(G)=n+1$?

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-22)

**Status:** open

**Assessment.** The exact two-scenario claim remains stated as a conjecture; rigidity-based maximum-likelihood-threshold results give substantial structure but do not establish this exhaustive classification.

**Sources checked.**

- [original OWR report](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2022/55)
